title: Kiosk registration and login (kiosk-pop)
description: The wire objects of Section 5: kiosk-pop, a proof-of-possession challenge-response. The caller proves that it holds the private key of the public key it presents, and the operator answers with a short-lived access token. The roots are open: they state what MUST be present and the shape of each member.

challenge.description: Section 5.1 -- the answer to GET <endpoint>/auth/challenge?public_key=<url-encoded PEM>. Single-use and short-lived; the nonce is worthless to anyone without the matching private key, which is why the endpoint is unauthenticated.
The server-issued nonce to sign. It becomes the `nonce` claim of the possession proof.

possessionProof.description: Section 5.2 -- the decoded payload of `signed`, a compact RS256 JWS. This is the object the register, login, claim and device-grant token calls all carry. It is a PAYLOAD, not a request body: the wire carries the compact serialisation, and this schema describes what a verifier reads out of it.

aud.description: ORIGIN-BINDING, and the reason a relayed proof is worthless. MUST be the origin the AI assistant dialed (Section 15.1); the operator rejects any other `aud`.

nonce.description: The `challenge` from Section 5.1. Single-use and server-TTL-bounded.

pub.description: RFC 7638 thumbprint of the public key; verified only when present.

iat.description: Informational only -- the server-issued `nonce` is the authoritative freshness bound, so an operator MUST NOT rely on this claim for freshness.

credentialRequest.description: Section 5.3 -- the body of POST /auth/register and POST /auth/login. Register also accepts an optional proof-of-work proof, which rides in the `Kiosk-PoW` request HEADER (Sections 5.5 and 10.1) and never in this body, so that the signed bytes are identical on the retry.

public_key.description: The AI assistant's public key, PEM-encoded. An AI assistant SHOULD generate a fresh keypair per operator origin (Section 15.3).

signed.description: The possession proof of Section 5.2, as a compact RS256 JWS. Its decoded payload is `#/$defs/possessionProof`.

registration.description: Section 5.3 -- the 201 answer to POST /auth/register. Registering an already-known key answers 409 conflict instead (use login). This is also the 201 answer to POST /auth/claim (Section 6.2), which is why `#/$defs/claimResponse` in binding.schema.json refers here rather than restating it.

agent_id.description: The acting agent id. Stable across a rebind (Section 6.3).

user_id.description: The identity the key maps to. An operator MUST map a known key to the same `user_id` so a saved payment card survives across sessions.

access_token.description: The access token, a compact RS256 JWT. Its claims are `#/$defs/accessTokenClaims`.

token.description: Section 5.3: the 200 answer to POST /auth/login; an unknown key answers 404 not_found. It is ALSO the 200 answer to POST /auth/revoke (Section 5.5) and to POST /auth/rotate (Section 5.7), with a token issued after the new watermark.

access_token.description: The access token, a compact RS256 JWT. Its claims are `#/$defs/accessTokenClaims`.

accessTokenClaims.description: Section 5.4 -- the decoded claim set of `access_token`. A 3-part RS256 JWT signed by the operator and verifiable statelessly against the JWKS of Section 4.4, bound to the identity's key and presented as `Authorization: DPoP` with a DPoP proof (Section 5.6).

actor.description: Always the string "agent". A token minted for anything else is not a Kiosk access token.

role.description: The role the operator assigns (Section 5.4). It is omitted when absent, never null. No endpoint accepts a role that the client requests.

aud.description: The operator issuer. A string, or the array spelling RFC 7519 permits.

iat.description: Issued-at. Also what the revoked-before watermark of Section 15.4 is compared against.

exp.description: Expiry. Default lifetime is 1 hour; the durable credential is the private key, not the token.

cnf.description: RFC 9449 Section 6.1 -- the key the token is bound to. Only a DPoP proof that this key signs makes the token usable.

jkt.description: The RFC 7638 thumbprint of the identity's registered key.

dpopProof.description: Section 5.6 -- the decoded payload of the `DPoP` request header, a compact RS256 JWS whose header carries `typ: "dpop+jwt"` and the public `jwk` of the registered key. The AI assistant signs a new one for each request that carries an access token.

jti.description: A unique id for this proof.

htm.description: The HTTP method of the request.

htu.description: The URL of the request, with no query and no fragment. On the event stream it is `events_url` with `wss` written as `https`.

iat.description: The time of signing. The operator refuses a proof more than 60 seconds from its clock.

ath.description: The base64url SHA-256 of the ASCII access token, with no padding.

rotationProof.description: Section 5.7 -- the decoded payload of `signed` in a rotation: a possession proof by the registered key that also names the new key.

rotationRequest.description: Section 5.7 -- the body of POST /auth/rotate. The answer is `#/$defs/token`, with a token bound to the new key.

signed.description: A possession proof by the registered key over a challenge issued for it. Its decoded payload is `#/$defs/rotationProof`.

new_public_key.description: The new key, PEM-encoded, in the key bounds of Section 5.1.

new_signed.description: A possession proof by the new key over a challenge issued for the new key. Its decoded payload is `#/$defs/possessionProof`.
